You'd probably have to use a separate proxy for each of the accounts. You could probably do thisneasy with Firefox and a plugin and a good list of reliable fast proxies.

Having a very large number of accounts, on the scale of 100's as opposed to 20, and then only using a few of them at a time for any particular post would make it harder to detect. You could also then change the useragent used by each account to make it appear as if they were all different people on different computers, even though they had the same IP address. As far as I know Reddit counts distinct users by a combination of their useragent and IP so this may work, but you could also use proxies to give a seperate IP to each account or group of accounts to make sure that there's no correlation. Of course at this stage it becomes very tedious to do by hand so a bot would be required.

It would help to have a number of IP addresses. Public proxies won't cut it, as these will already be on Reddit's radar; your best bet would be computers you have compromised (i.e. a small bot net). Each should have an account registered with a unique email address (Gmail or similar would work well). The accounts should be created at different times (i.e. not all at once). Only a subset should upvote/downvote in any given thread that you want to manipulate (say 5%), and it should be a different combination each time (just use a stochastic trigger). The accounts need to be active at times other than when manipulating (i.e. they should be upvoting and downvoting other threads, and potentially commenting on threads or submitting content). Never log into the accounts from any computer other than the dedicated one (i.e. so that the IPs aren't connectible, and no flags are raised by accounts being logged into from different countries or whatever). Ideally, the accounts should show human-like behaviour (i.e. their interaction should be with a specific set of subs which happen to overlap with the ones you want to manipulate; their interaction with the website should be at certain times of the day or days of the week, etc.). The other thing to bear in mind is the 'hot' algorithm that Reddit uses (i.e. it's not just about the number of votes something receives, but the temporal proximity of those votes). By-and-large, your goal isn't to do all the work on your own, it's to either get a thread/comment noticed (so the community does the rest of the upvoting), or bury it quickly so it gets no upvotes.
